source: NIST SRD 141, Atomic Reference Data for Electronic Structure Calculations (Kotochigova, Levine, Shirley, Stiles, Clark, Phys. Rev. A 55, 191 (1997); erratum 56, 5191), https://www.nist.gov/pml/atomic-reference-data-electronic-structure-calculations -- neutral-atom tables, ScRLDA column. Per-element pages: https://www.nist.gov/pml/atomic-reference-data-electronic-structure-calculations/atomic-reference-data-electronic-7-{8,16,35,52,63,64,70,90} (Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Au, Hg, Rn, U), reached from the index at https://www.nist.gov/pml/atomic-reference-data-electronic-structure-calculations/atomic-reference-data-electronic-7. Method facts confirmed on the Procedure page https://www.nist.gov/pml/atomic-reference-data-electronic-structure-calculations/atomic-reference-data-electronic-3 on 2026-10-03: 'In the RLDA and ScRLDA calculations, we use the relativistic corrections to the energy-density functional proposed by MacDonald and Vosko'; VWN correlation throughout; alpha^-1 = 137.0359895 (1986 CODATA); j occupation proportional to 2j+1 ('if there were 2 electrons in a p shell, we assign an electron population of 4/3 to the p3/2 states and 2/3 to the p1/2 states'). The Procedure page never mentions a nuclear model; treated here as a point nucleus per the plan's solver. Kr 4p row: NIST's page prints the RLDA 4p+ cell as '-0.33742' (one digit short of the table's 6-decimal format; recorded as -0.337420) and the ScRLDA 4p cell as '-0.345161 3' (an untagged trailing digit with no footnote; dropped). The missing sixth digit is not independently confirmed: treat that value as good to the published 5 decimals. Both anomalies are unique to this row across the eight pages.
